messages:
infra-bot: ALERT: shared-pool-eu-gpu queue depth 138, 95th latency spike 1.2s, affected tenants: multiple. auto-ratecap engaged.

maria: seeing this now, looks like a burst from a single tenant (atlas-ml) running many long-context batches at once :eyes:

ajay: confirming — atlas-ml caused KV cache thrash. their KV size jumped 8x in 20m and we started evicting hot entries, causing token regen and longer runtimes.

sam: ugh. this is classic noisy-neighbor in shared pools. we need a quick soft-quota experiment that enforces backpressure but keeps short bursts. not hard preemption.

kevin: agree. proposal: dynamic soft-quota that reduces per-tenant burst credits as pool queue depth increases, plus a fast-path for small interactive requests. idea sketch: 
```yaml
admission:
  pool: shared-eu-gpu
  mode: dynamic-soft-quota
  queue_threshold: 100  # start applying when queued requests > 100
  base_burst_credits: 2000
  burst_decay_factor: 0.6  # multiply credits by this when threshold breached
  interactive_window_ms: 200  # requests < 200ms considered interactive, bypass soft quota
  min_rate_qps: 0.2
```

maria: +1 to that config. interactive window keeps chat snappy. also add a per-tenant token-accounting metric so we can track who consumed burst credits and why.

lia: we should simulate first. I can replay last 2 hours of traces for shared-eu and run the admission controller offline to measure impact on tail latency and throughput. will need a tagged run for atlas-ml to see fairness delta.

ajay: one more detail: KV cache eviction policy should be slightly more conservative for tenants currently being rate-limited so we don't punish them twice. suggestion: mark evicted keys with tenant_rate_limited flag and lower eviction priority for 30s.

sam: good point. also consider soft-cache-eviction: instead of immediate drop remove 10% each second while under limit. softer than full purge.

kevin: what about cost tradeoffs? If we throttle heavy tenants earlier we may push more work to dedicated customers or cause retries. need a quick calc: reduce burst credits by 40% -> estimated 22% drop in peak GPU utilization, ~8% savings in infra spend on that pool for the hour, but potential 0.5% revenue impact if customer experiences errors.

maria: we'll capture error budget delta and customer-facing latency change. canary plan: enable dynamic-soft-quota in eu-west shared pool for 2h during low-traffic window, keep metrics dashboard and circuit-breaker to revert instantly.

lia: test plan checklist:
- replay trace with and without controller (offline)
- small canary: 5% of traffic redirected to controller (1h)
- full canary: 100% shared-eu for 2h with rollback script
- collect: per-tenant queued_tokens, 95/99 latency, cache-eviction-rate, failed-requests

maria: assigning: lia -> replay & canary infra, ajay -> cache eviction changes, sam -> admission controller config, kevin -> cost/risk calc, i'll own rollback and comms. target tomorrow 09:00 UTC for replay results.

kevin: quick note: add a temporary label for atlas-ml so SRE + CS can reach out if they see functional regressions.

ajay: implemented preliminary eviction tweak in staging, pushing to canary branch now. log snippet: 
```
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] tenant=atlas-ml kv_size=1.2GB evict_policy=soft tag=tenant_rate_limited=true
[2026-03-18T09:12:04Z] admission=soft-quota applied burst_credits=1200 -> 720 queue_pos=34
```

maria: perfect. if replay looks good we flip 5% canary at 10:00 UTC. please post results in this thread. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: NOTE: canary flag created: feature/soft-quota-eu, rollback window 30m.

sam: small UX caveat — document that edge-case: long-running batch jobs may see higher latency; CS should be able to request temporary exceptions (temporary dedicated capacity) rather than full removal.

lia: replay started, ETA ~45m. posting interim KPIs to dashboards/shared when ready.

maria: thanks team. let’s try to avoid hard eviction or token draining that can cascade across regions. keep it soft and observable. :thinking:
